subject: English
subskill: Meaning of Word in Literary Prose
passage:
The following text is adapted from a 1921 play by Ingrid Graves.

MARGOT: Listen to me, Bilal, listen! I may look composed, I may speak calmly, but I have undergone so much this year! I've been cold, I've been hungry, I've been turned away from every door—misfortune has chased me down every road I've taken!
prompt: As used in the text, what does the word "undergone" most nearly mean?
explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because as used in the text, 'undergone' most nearly means experienced. Margot describes the hardships she has lived through, stating that she has been 'cold,' 'hungry,' and 'turned away from every door,' and that 'misfortune has chased [her] down every road.' These details indicate that Margot has experienced, or lived through and endured, 'so much' difficulty.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. Although 'undergone' might in some contexts relate to transmitting something, it doesn't mean conveyed, or communicated, in this context. Margot is not talking about communicating hardships to Bilal but rather describing the difficult experiences she has personally lived through.
